title: assembly-panel
content:
Assembly Panel

The Assembly panel (titled Assembly Workflow) is used to define and play back step-by-step assembly or disassembly sequences with smooth GSAP animations, and to save/recall named poses of the scene. It has four main sub-sections: Workflows, States, Playback and Edit.

Workflows

A scene can hold several alternative assembly procedures over the same parts, so you can try out different orders without deleting the one you already have. Only one workflow can be active at a time, because steps physically move the objects in the viewport.

  • Active workflow – Selects the workflow that Playback, Edit and the step list operate on. Switching returns all objects to the fully assembled position first.

  • + New workflow – Creates an empty workflow and makes it active.

  • ⧉ Duplicate workflow – Copies the active workflow with all its steps and makes the copy active. Use this to experiment with a variant while keeping the original intact.

  • ✎ Rename workflow – Renames the active workflow.

  • ✕ Delete workflow – Deletes the active workflow. When only one workflow is left it is emptied instead of removed.

The assembled (start) position of each part is shared by all workflows — editing it in one procedure updates the others as well. All workflows are saved into the GLB file and restored on load. Importing a model that already contains workflows adds them as new entries, so nothing is ever overwritten. The self-contained HTML export contains only the active workflow.

States

A state is a named snapshot of where things currently are — the position, rotation, scale and visibility of every part, and optionally the camera view — independent of any workflow or step. Use states when you care about a particular configuration of the assembly (e.g. "exploded view for the manual", "maintenance access position") rather than the procedure used to reach it. States are global to the scene, shared by all workflows.

  • Status – Read-only label showing the selected state, e.g. 2: Exploded, or – not applied – if none is selected yet. Once the scene changes — a manual drag, or navigating/animating the assembly workflow — the label switches to 2: Exploded (modified) to show the scene no longer exactly matches the saved snapshot. The selection itself is kept, so the state can still be updated, renamed, duplicated or deleted.

  • + Capture current – Prompts for a name and saves the current pose of every part as a new state.

  • ↻ Update active – Overwrites the selected state with the scene's current pose (this is how a "(modified)" scene is saved back into the same state) and clears the modified flag. Disabled unless a captured (non-Initial) state is selected.

  • ✎ Rename – Renames the selected state.

  • ⧉ Duplicate – Copies the selected state (or Initial if none is selected) and makes the copy the new selection.

  • ✕ Delete – Deletes the selected state. The built-in Initial state cannot be deleted.

  • ✕ Delete all… – Deletes every captured state, keeping only Initial. Requires confirmation.

  • 📷 Save camera view / ✕ Clear camera view – Attaches or removes the current camera position/target/zoom from the selected state, so applying it later can optionally move the camera too (subject to the Camera toggle in Playback).

  • Saved states (N) – Dynamic list with one button per state, including the built-in Initial state (the as-loaded pose). The selected state is marked with ▶ (matches the scene exactly) or ● (modified since it was applied). Clicking a button instantly applies that state, animating the camera if it has a saved view. Applying a state is undoable like any other scene change.

States are saved into the GLB file (per-object poses plus a name/order index) and restored on load; importing a model that already contains states adds them to the existing catalog. Moving an object manually, or navigating/animating the assembly workflow, marks the selected state "(modified)" rather than deselecting it, since the scene no longer necessarily matches the saved snapshot exactly — use ↻ Update active to save the new pose into it, or + Capture current to save it as a separate state instead.

Playback

Controls for navigating and animating the assembly sequence.

  • Status – Read-only label showing the current playback position (e.g. Step 2 / 5 – Attach lid).

  • Loop ∞ (start ↔ finish) – When checked, the animation loops continuously between the start and finish positions.

  • Camera 🎥 (animate camera) – When checked, the camera moves to the saved view for each step during animated playback.

  • Zoom coeff 🔍 (ortho only) – Scaling coefficient (0.1–5.0) applied to the orthographic camera zoom during camera animation. Has no effect in perspective mode.

  • ⏮ Reset to start [Home] – Instantly moves all objects to their fully assembled position (before step 1). Keyboard shortcut: Home.

  • ◀◀ Animate to start [Shift+PgUp] – Plays the animation backward to the start position. Keyboard shortcut: Shift+PageUp.

  • ◀ Previous step [PageUp] – Steps one step backward. Keyboard shortcut: PageUp.

  • Next step ▶ [PageDown] – Steps one step forward. Keyboard shortcut: PageDown.

  • Animate to finish ▶▶ [Shift+PgDn] – Plays the animation forward to the last step. Keyboard shortcut: Shift+PageDown.

  • Reset to finish ⏭ [End] – Instantly moves all objects to their fully disassembled position (after the last step). Keyboard shortcut: End.

Animation Settings

Fine-grained GSAP tween parameters applied to all step animations.

  • Duration (ms) – Length of each step animation in milliseconds (0–2000).

  • Ease – GSAP easing function applied to every object movement. Options include none, power1–4, back, bounce, elastic, circ, expo, sine, each with .in, .out, and .inOut variants.

  • Repeat (-1=∞) – Number of times each step animation repeats. -1 = infinite.

  • Delay (ms) – Pause before each animation starts (0–2000 ms).

  • Repeat delay (ms) – Pause between repetitions (0–2000 ms).

  • Yoyo – When checked, each repeat plays the animation in reverse (forward → back → forward…).

  • Stagger (ms) – Time offset between individual object animations within the same step (0–1000 ms). Creates a cascading effect.

  • Overwrite – GSAP overwrite mode: auto (smart conflict resolution), true (kill all previous tweens on target), or false (no overwrite).

Edit

Tools for creating and modifying assembly steps. All controls except Edit mode are disabled until edit mode is activated.

  • Edit mode – Enables assembly editing. When active, moving a named object in the viewport records its new position as a transformation for the currently active step. On step 0: Assembled, the same drag updates the object's assembled start position instead (disassembled / final positions stay unchanged). Objects not in any step are not added to the workflow.

  • Edit assembled [Home] – Jumps to the fully assembled state and enables edit mode. Moving a named object that already belongs to the workflow records its new position as the assembled start.

  • Edit disassembled [End] – Jumps to the fully disassembled state and enables edit mode. Moving a named object records its new position as the final (disassembled) position of the step that already contains that object, rather than always writing into the last step.

  • Active step – Read-only label indicating which step is currently being edited.

  • Step name – Editable name for the active step, shown in the Status label during playback.

  • Description – Optional free-text description for the active step.

  • + New step – Creates a new empty step after the current position.

  • ✕ Delete step – Removes the currently active step and all its recorded transformations.

  • ✕ Delete all steps… – Removes every step of the active workflow and all its recorded transformations, then returns objects to the fully assembled position. Requires confirmation.

  • ↑ Move step up – Moves the active step one position earlier in the sequence.

  • ↓ Move step down – Moves the active step one position later in the sequence.

  • ✕ Remove object from step – Removes the currently selected object's transformation from the active step (the object will no longer move during that step).

  • 📷 Save camera view – Stores the current camera position and orientation as the camera view for the active step. Used during animated playback when Camera is enabled.

  • ✕ Clear camera view – Removes the saved camera view from the active step.

Workflow: Creating an Assembly

  1. Load the fully assembled model.

  2. Open the Assembly panel and switch to Edit mode.

  3. Click + New step. Give the step a name.

  4. Select an object and drag it to its disassembled position. The transformation is recorded automatically.

  5. Repeat steps 3–4 for each assembly step.

  6. Use the Playback controls to review the animation.

  7. To try an alternative order, use ⧉ Duplicate workflow and rearrange the steps in the copy. The original stays untouched and you can switch between them at any time.

  8. Save the model via the File panel to embed the assembly data of all workflows.
